correctness.rationale: On the mean-zero subspace, adding a nonnegative rank-one Laplacian shifts the second eigenvalue at most to the original third eigenvalue \(2-2\cos(2\pi/n)\). If the new-edge vector has nonzero projection onto the original third mode, a two-mode test vector in its nullspace has Rayleigh quotient strictly below this ceiling; cosine equality forces \(i+j=n-1\). For centered chords reflection decomposes the operator. The antisymmetric shifted block has one negative eigenvalue and is invertible. Its explicit piecewise sine/cosine resolvent yields \(b^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}b=-\sin((2i+1)2\pi/n)/\sin(2\pi/n)\). The block-matrix Schur-complement inertia criterion gives positive semidefiniteness iff \(w\sin((2i+1)2\pi/n)\ge\sin(2\pi/n)\) with positive sine. Maximizing over centered odd indices and checking equality yields the stated sharp minimum and optimizer count. All boundary quantifiers include n=4. The verifier ran 6,611 finite eigenvalue, threshold and resolvent checks; it is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The mathematically natural control resource problem asks how weak a single extra conductance can be while still achieving the highest spectral gap allowed by any rank-one Laplacian perturbation. The proof obtains a nontrivial complete family of feasible saturating links, a sharp exact minimum-cost threshold, an exact count of all unit-cost optimal links, and the asymptotic \(2\pi/n\) threshold. These are motivated structural answers beyond a textbook interlacing inequality or arbitrary finite example; the unsolved below-threshold regime is correctly excluded.
